name: Suzlon Energy Ltd
tagline: Completed debt-free turnaround with a large domestic wind order book (6.1 GW) and a capital-light DevCo model now driving ~60% of new FY27 orders - a genuine named inflection for a large-cap, but not a literal 10x/100x case at this size.
business_overview: Suzlon Energy is India's largest domestic wind turbine OEM (manufacturing, EPC and O&M), historically debt-laden through the mid-2010s to early 2020s, now past a multi-year balance-sheet restructuring. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@rdkriplani, bullish view, medium conviction, 2026-09-13).
fundamentals_table: Revenue CAGR ~64.65% (industry median ~44.6%); FY26 revenue +54% YoY to Rs 16,679 Cr
Almost debt-free; net worth ~Rs 9,869 Cr; net cash position ~Rs 2,322 Cr
~6.1 GW order book; >1.1 GW new orders booked in FY27 so far, ~60% via the DevCo (asset-light) model; highest-ever Q1 deliveries (506 MW, +14% YoY)
fundamentals_narrative: Suzlon has completed a genuine, named structural turnaround: from chronically debt-laden to a net-cash balance sheet (~Rs 2,322 Cr net cash, ~Rs 9,869 Cr net worth), with ROCE/ROE now at 34%/40% and revenue growing 54-65% CAGR off a large domestic order book (~6.1 GW). The DevCo model - originating a majority of new FY27 orders (~60%) on an asset-light basis - is a specific, named commercial-model shift worth treating as an inflection rather than routine growth. At ~19x trailing P/E against this growth/return profile, the stock is not obviously expensive, though it already trades well off its 52-week high, suggesting some of the turnaround is priced in. At a ~Rs 60,000 Cr market cap, a literal 10x (to ~Rs 6 lakh Cr) or 100x is not a credible framing regardless of operating strength - this is a large-cap turnaround/growth compounder, not an early-stage small-cap.
technical_read: Trading near Rs 44, roughly mid-range of the Rs 38.2-61.5 52-week band, off the highs - not independently verified against a moving-average filter this pass.

Large, growing order book (~6.1 GW) with a capital-light DevCo model now sourcing ~60% of new FY27 orders
Revenue CAGR ~54-65%, highest-ever Q1 FY27 deliveries - genuine operating momentum, not just balance-sheet repair
Valuation (~19x P/E) not stretched relative to the growth/return profile
